article_text:
Tom Cruise dá presença à sátira de Alejandro G.z Iñárritu, mas a reflexão sobre os limites da arte diante da catástrofe perde força entre explicações excessivas e personagens pouco desenvolvidos.

“ Digger ” está ciente do risco de espetacularizar uma catástrofe, e faz desse incômodo parte da sua narrativa. Alejandro González Iñárritu utiliza a sátira como uma maneira de discutir as histórias que nos permitem conviver com desastres sem enfrentar suas causas — incluindo nessa suspeita o próprio filme. Essa disposição para examinar seus limites rende uma proposta mais instigante do que os conflitos e personagens que deveriam sustentá-la.

Tom Cruise interpreta Digger Rockwell, um empresário cuja exploração do Ártico desencadeia um desastre ambiental. Depois de minimizar uma rachadura na plataforma de gelo, ele precisa lidar com uma massa desprendida da Groenlândia que avança em direção à Europa. Sua mansão passa a receber autoridades interessadas em administrar a crise, entre elas o presidente dos Estados Unidos (John Goodman), enquanto as discussões sobre uma possível intervenção nuclear expõem uma preocupação persistente com as consequências pessoais de qualquer decisão.

Antes mesmo dessas reuniões, o espaço já conta bastante sobre o protagonista. O design de produção idealiza uma residência onde pinturas ocupam o lugar de janelas e espelhos multiplicam a imagem do proprietário. Digger se cerca de representações que pode controlar, protegido de um mundo cujos líderes vão visitá-lo, e não o contrário. Essa organização visual é uma maneira eficiente de mostrar seu autoengano ao tratar a dimensão da catástrofe como se também pudesse ajustá-la às proporções que lhe convêm.

A maquiagem modifica o rosto e o corpo de Cruise, mas o ator vai além ao aplicar sua habitual energia a uma figura decadente e convencida da própria importância. É interessante vê-lo usar essa intensidade num papel tão distante de Ethan Hunt ou Maverick. No discurso diante do parlamento europeu, uma longa tomada acompanha seus movimentos numa espécie de coreografia, enquanto Digger denuncia a dependência coletiva do petróleo para apresentar a si mesmo como indispensável. Iñárritu, porém, prolonga a argumentação depois que a manobra já está compreendida, explicando a piada até desgastar seu efeito.

Ao redor dele, a sátira política opera quase sempre no registro mais explícito. O presidente de Goodman e os demais participantes das reuniões chegam definidos por personalidades grotescas tomadas pela vaidade e pela irresponsabilidade. A aproximação com “Dr. Fantástico” surge nessa combinação de poder militar, ego e destruição. As interações, porém, pouco revelam além do despreparo anunciado desde a apresentação dessas autoridades. Michael Stuhlbarg, subaproveitado como o vice-presidente, exemplifica a pouca margem concedida ao elenco.

Uma mudança de perspectiva coloca essa caricatura sob suspeita ao sugerir que reduzir os responsáveis pelo desastre a figuras ridículas também pode ser uma maneira de manter a realidade à distância. O humor cede espaço a uma abordagem bem mais sóbria, acompanhada por um conflito pessoal que tenta aproximar a ameaça de uma experiência íntima do protagonista. Contudo, o filme pede envolvimento com esse drama pessoal antes de desenvolver os vínculos que poderiam torná-lo significativo. As passagens dedicadas a isso acabam soando como interrupções, sem estabelecer um envolvimento capaz de equilibrar essa alternância.

A fotografia de Emmanuel Lubezki encontra variações expressivas no contraste entre a vastidão fria do desastre e os interiores decadentes da elite dominante, dando escala àquilo que as reuniões tentam administrar de dentro de espaços fechados. Nas mudanças de perspectiva, a luz altera nossa percepção dos ambientes e põe em dúvida a aparência que eles haviam assumido. Em conjunto com o design de produção, esse trabalho permite experimentar visualmente a instabilidade das representações.

O desfecho amplia a dimensão do desastre e procura aproximar o universo do filme da experiência de quem o assiste. A revelação final surpreende pela escala da catástrofe, mas seu impacto fica limitado pelo pouco interesse que os personagens despertam.

“Digger” encontra uma boa questão nas histórias usadas para tornar a realidade suportável. Ao colocar sua própria sátira sob suspeita, porém, Iñárritu abre possibilidades que os personagens e suas relações sustentam apenas em parte. A lucidez da proposta não basta para dar força dramática ao conjunto. O filme percebe a armadilha, explica seu funcionamento e permanece dentro dela.

François Pinault über seine Sammlung, Louvre-Direktor warnt vor Schließung des Museums und der Mythos von Leonardo da Vinci als Universalgenie: Das ist unsere Medienschau am Donnerstag

Museen

Louvre-Direktor Christophe Leribault warnt im "Figaro" : Das meistbesuchte Museum der Welt drohe ohne eine grundlegende Sanierung zu schließen. "Wer auch immer die nächste Regierung bildet, muss bedenken, dass der Louvre sehr schnell ins Hintertreffen gerät und irgendwann seine Türen für die Öffentlichkeit schließen muss, wenn er nicht repariert, modernisiert und umgebaut wird. Das wäre eine Katastrophe", sagte er. Leribault, der nach dem Juwelenraub vom 19. Oktober 2025 im Februar sein Amt antrat, setzt auf private Geldgeber, verlangt aber nach den nächstjährigen Wahlen zusätzlich öffentliche Mittel. Einen 83 Millionen Euro teuren Sicherheitsplan treibe er "zügig" voran. Es gebe jedoch keine einfache "Wunderlösung" an der Oberfläche: "Alles hängt zusammen." Gewerkschaften kritisierten zuvor Präsident Macrons 600-Millionen-Plan samt neuem Eingang als überdimensioniert. Außerdem im "Figaro" : Der ehemalige Polizeikommissar Olivier Goupil, der diesen Sommer sein Amt als Sicherheitskoordinator des Louvre angetreten hat, erklärt, wie er sich auf Bedrohungen vorbereitet.

Nordkoreas Machthaber Kim Jong Un hat ein Museum für nationale Verteidigungsrevolution eingeweiht. Wie Fotos zeigen , war auch Kims Tochter mit dabei, die der südkoreanische Geheimdienst NIS für dessen politische Nachfolgerin hält und die zuletzt immer wieder bei offiziellen Terminen mit ihrem Vater auftrat. Weitere Aufnahmen des Museums zeigen verschiedene dort ausgestellte Raketentypen. Laut Südkoreas amtlicher Nachrichtenagentur Yonhap befand sich darunter auch die "Hwasong 20"-Interkontinentalrakete, bei der davon ausgegangen wird, dass sie das US-Festland erreichen könnte.

Kunstmarkt

Im "Le Monde"-Interview spricht François Pinault über seine Sammlung zeitgenössischer Kunst, die mehr als 10.000 Werke umfasst. Ab März 2027 sollen im Palazzo Grassi in Venedig dauerhaft 106 Werke von 54 Künstlerinnen und Künstlern zu sehen sein . Nach 20 Jahren mit Wechselausstellungen wolle er damit wichtige Arbeiten zusammenführen, die "durch ihre Kraft und ihre Fähigkeit, die Zeit zu überdauern", zu Marksteinen ihrer Epoche geworden seien. Eine endgültige Lesart der Sammlung sei damit nicht beabsichtigt: "Unser Blick auf die Kunst entwickelt sich ständig weiter." Pinault betont, dass er seine Sammlung nicht nach kunsthistorischen Programmen zusammenstelle, sondern sich von Begegnungen und persönlichen Vorlieben leiten lasse. Sie sei "zutiefst subjektiv" und oft aus Instinkt, Leidenschaft oder sogar aus Wut über die Gewalt der Gegenwart entstanden. Kunst interessiere ihn, weil sie die Wirklichkeit spiegeln, auf Distanz zu ihr gehen und die "tiefe Instabilität der Gegenwart" sichtbar machen könne. Auf die Frage, ob er ein eher tragisches Weltbild habe, antwortet der Unternehmer: "Schwarz, tragisch oder realistisch. Man darf mir nicht erzählen, dass die Welt erfreulich ist."

Ausstellung

In der "SZ" beschreibt Alexander Menden die Ausstellung "Haus u r 2026" von Gregor Schneider in der Kunsthalle Düsseldorf . Seit vier Jahrzehnten verwandelt der Künstler sein Elternhaus in Mönchengladbach-Rheydt in ein immer weiter wachsendes Labyrinth aus verschobenen Türen, Fluren und Zimmern. Die Düsseldorfer Ausstellung versammelt 17 Raumrepliken, darunter zehn identische Badezimmer, die nur einzeln betreten werden dürfen. Schneider wehrt sich gegen die Vorstellung, seine Räume seien eine Art Gruselkabinett: "Es ist keine Geisterbahn, sondern die Möglichkeit, über Räume nachzudenken." Die Beklemmung entstehe auch durch die Besucher selbst, die Zimmer als "Zellen und Rattenkäfige" wahrnähmen, sich zugleich aber mit ihrer Funktion arrangierten. Den besonderen Reiz sieht Menden in der Loslösung der Räume von ihrem ursprünglichen Zusammenhang: Wo immer man sie betrete, befinde man sich "in der Schneider-Welt". Die Ausstellung ist bis zum 17. Januar 2027 zu sehen.

Kunstgeschichte

In der "London Review of Books" hinterfragt Charles Hope den Mythos von Leonardo da Vinci als Universalgenie . In seiner Besprechung von Stephen J. Campbells Biografie "Leonardo da Vinci: An Untraceable Life" schreibt Hope, Leonardo verdanke seinen heutigen Ruhm nicht allein seiner Kunst. Entscheidend seien auch die massenhafte Verbreitung von Reproduktionen, der Tourismus und die Vermarktung seiner Person. Campbell spreche von "Da-Vinci-Welten", in denen Leonardo zur Ware geworden sei. Selbst die Kunstgeschichte trage zur Legendenbildung bei: Sie habe das Bild eines singulären Genies geprägt, dessen Interessen von Anatomie bis Maschinenbau reichten. Hope hält dagegen, viele seiner Forschungen seien für die Malerei kaum relevant gewesen. Leonardo habe zudem regelmäßig mit Assistenten und Mitarbeitern gearbeitet. Seine besondere Wirkung auf Zeitgenossen sei wohl weniger seiner Wissenschaft als seinem musikalischen Talent, seinem Humor und seiner Erfindungsgabe zu verdanken gewesen. Ein Beispiel sei der mechanische Löwe gewesen, der sich vor König Franz I. verbeugt und eine Lilienblüte aus seiner Brust präsentiert haben soll. Zwar sei Campbells These überzeugend, Leonardo stärker als Produkt seiner Zeit zu betrachten – doch, so Hope, "die meisten Menschen, darunter viele Kunsthistoriker, bevorzugen einen attraktiven Mythos gegenüber der prosaischen Wirklichkeit".

Lorsqu’on le rencontre à Cannes, sa sympathie, son aisance à l’oral et sa facilité à articuler ses idées – qu’on devine bouillonnantes – marquent immédiatement. « Je suis comme Toni sur ce plan », admet-il après une pause. « Je réfléchis beaucoup, mais je suis aussi très contradictoire. Je peux penser des choses et tout l’inverse en même temps. »

Marine Atlan : « J’ai traversé des choses assez profondes de mon histoire avec « La Gradiva » »

Au départ, ce créatif qui, selon ses dires, n’était « pas très bon à l’école, sauf en maths », se destinait à une carrière de danseur. Au collège, puis au lycée, il se spécialise en section hip-hop, avant d’arrêter subitement la danse après huit années pour des raisons personnelles. « C’est comme ça, c’est la vie », conclut-il, magnanime. Né dans une famille d’intermittents du spectacle, il envisage un moment une formation en économie, précisant « le mot “artiste” est accompagné de névroses, je n’avais pas du tout envie d’aller vers ça ». Mais, lors d’un voyage scolaire en terminale à Naples, il rencontre la réalisatrice française, venue en observation pour développer le scénario de son premier long métrage.

Des dizaines de castings et beaucoup d’hésitations plus tard, Colas Quignard accepte d’endosser le rôle délicat de Toni et se passionne pour le jeu d’acteur. « J’ai retrouvé dans le cinéma ce que j’aimais dans la danse . J’aime le fait d’être dirigé, de devoir comprendre où on veut m’emmener, d’essayer des choses et de me tromper. » Inscrit depuis au conservatoire de théâtre, il a trouvé sa voie : « Ce que je veux faire, c’est jouer, habiter un personnage et me documenter sur plein de sujets. » On ne demande qu’à voir la suite.*

article_text:
Battered Netflix shares tumbled in after-hours trading Tuesday as the company lowered full-year advertising guidance and issued an updated revenue outlook that disappointed Wall Street.

The swoon came despite a solid set of financials for the third quarter. Earnings per share of 87 cents beat Wall Street expectations, rising from 59 cents in the same period of 2025. Revenue of $12.87 billion, up 12% year-over-year, matched the Street estimate.

Related Stories

Skeptical Wall Street Dings Netflix On Soft Revenue Forecast

Netflix Layoffs Underway, Streamer Cutting 1,000 Jobs, 6% Of Workforce

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue to rise 12% to $13.4 billion, while full-year revenue is now projected to come in at $51.1 billion. While that would be 13% above 2025 levels, the new forecast is slightly below analysts’ consensus and also at the low end of the range the company provided in prior earnings reports. Higher expenses, meanwhile, including those related to the recent layoff of about 1,000 workers , will also squeeze operating margins.

Watch on Deadline

Advertising revenue is now projected to be $2.7 billion for 2026, compared with earlier forecasts for $3 billion. In its quarterly letter to shareholders, the company blamed the reduction on “slightly slower than expected rollout of some ad product capabilities.”

The results come on the heels of last week’s layoffs , the company’s deepest cuts since 2022, as well as the ouster of high-level executives including content chief Bela Bajaria . Co-CEO Ted Sarandos recently said at a conference that viewership on Netflix hasn’t been growing “as fast as I want,” and the executive overhaul is perhaps a prelude to larger strategic changes as the company plots a new course.

RELATED: Ted Sarandos Praises Axed Bela Bajaria On Eve Of Peter Rice’s Netflix Debut

“We know there’s some investor concern about our view hours growth,” the shareholder letter said. “Member response to our 2026 price increases is consistent with prior price changes and our expectations, an indicator that our engagement – which encompasses quantity, quality and variety of viewing – remains healthy and that we continue to deliver strong value to members. But we do seek to accelerate growth in view hours as well.”

The letter listed a number of notable originals from outside the U.S., noting that non-English viewing has grown from less than 10% of total viewing to more than one-third today. The name-checked series included Plastic Beauty , The Secret Woman and The Perfect Lie , which are on track to become the most-watched titles ever in Japan, Denmark and the Netherlands, respectively. Facing El Chapo is on course to be the No. 2 Mexican title across the global service’s 325 million subscribers.

In the U.S., however, the company has been moving sideways as competitors have managed more impressive runs in 2026. Along with its main linear and streaming rivals, Netflix has been frustrated by YouTube, which has been the No. 1 destination in streaming for three years running.

Netflix has faced trying times before over its entire existence. When it lit up its website as a startup company, the servers crashed. After successfully scaling its DVD rental business, in 2011 it proposed spinning it out into a separate company called Qwikster, a scheme that tanked the stock and got spoofed on Saturday Night Live . And in 2022, the great Netflix correction saw the company jump into advertising after years of denying it would as a way to counteract the narrative about its then-stagnating subscriber growth.

In the current moment, there are a few factors that have combined to send the stock down 40% over the past year. Chief among them is its slowing viewership growth of late, a trend that prompted last week’s replacement of Bajaria with Peter Rice .

RELATED: Netflix Shakeup: Peter Rice Is Welcomed Back To Executive Ranks While Bela Bajaria’s Exit Has Layoff-Weary Staff Bracing For More Upheaval

Another is the lingering shock of its decision to enter the high-stakes chase for Warner Bros, which top execs drew skepticism by declaring a “‘nice-to-have, not a need-to-have'” asset. After clinching a deal to acquire Warner’s studio-and-streaming division last December in by far its biggest ever M&A deal, it ultimately was dislodged by Paramount, which offered $110 billion for all of Warner Bros. Discovery.

article_text:
The release of Laika ‘s “ Wildwood ” at the box office this weekend was about more than just the dollars and cents or the success or failure of a single film ; in some ways it was about the future of a fan-favorite film studio.

“Wildwood” is the Portland, Oregon-based stop-motion animation studio’s sixth animated feature but also the first movie released by the studio in seven years. Easily director Travis Knight’s most ambitious project to date under the Laika banner, it’s been in the works for even longer than that time gap: fans have been awaiting it for years. Heck, we’ve been talking about this movie since last year .

What Laika needed with “Wildwood” was not just a solid number but a display of genuine enthusiasm that this movie could reintroduce audiences to the studio. Even if a movie like “ Coraline ,” Laika’s debut, breakout stop-motion hit, was not a gangbusters blockbuster upon its release, it’s a film that has had real staying power and made a legacy for Laika in the process.

“Wildwood” grossed $12.2 million domestic in its opening weekend, placing it at No. 3 for the weekend behind “Clayface” and “You Can See Everything. It also added an additional $2.9 million from a handful of international markets and still has a lot to go. Those aren’t eye-popping numbers, and when you hear reports that the budget is around $100 million (with some others suggesting it could be one of the most expensive animated movies ever made ), it’s not a surprise that many of the headlines surrounding “Wildwood” are that it could be a big money loser .

But having expensive, hand-crafted passion projects that view budgets as an after-thought are kind of part of Laika’s DNA . And it’s clear after one weekend that “Wildwood” is not the let down its previous feature, 2019’s “Missing Link,” turned out to be. That film opened to less than half of what “Wildwood” did with just $5.9 million and finished at $17 million domestic, a number “Wildwood” will easily surpass.

The better comp for “Wildwood” is “Kubo and the Two Strings,” which opened to $12.6 million and finished with $48 million domestic and $76 million worldwide. It’s also not far off from DreamWorks’ “Forgotten Island” from earlier this year, which opened to $13 million and has made $67.9 million worldwide thus far.

The key though is for “Wildwood” to repeat the stellar holds and word of mouth over time that some of its past hits have done. All five of its previous films have had hefty multiples, including “Coraline” (4.5x), “ParaNorman” (4.1x), and “Kubo and the Two Strings” (3.8x). A 3.8 multiple for “Wildwood,” same as “Kubo,” would have it finish with roughly $46.3 million domestic.

Some of the early exit tracking suggests it has a chance to be even better than that. “Wildwood” received an A CinemaScore and almost universal positive scores and “recommend” grades from PostTrak, in addition to a 99 percent on Rotten Tomatoes at time of writing. It had strong per-screen-averages across 395 PLFs and some Dolby Cinemas in particular, and it even packed houses in places like Portland where the film is set and pays homage.

Dave Burke, Laika’s Chief Marketing Officer and an EP on the film, told IndieWire those figures suggest it could even add a few screens beyond the 2,940 it had this first weekend. Alamo Drafthouse for one played the film on 11 screens and is looking to add another six, Burke said. Also of note is that this is one of Fathom Entertainment’s first truly wide releases for an original film after having big success re-releasing “Coraline,” so both companies are viewing these numbers as encouraging.

“I think we needed to prove ourselves as the new kid on the block, and I think the data points to the fact that there’s a really compelling business case for exhibition to get on even more robustly and support the film in the kind of coming weeks,” Burke said.

Many of Laika’s films have been darker in nature, and “Wildwood” does not shy away from that. The studio has been upfront in its marketing that the film is PG-13, that it aims to reach a general audience rather than kids, and is based on a middlegrade novel from Colin Meloy, better known as the lead singer of the indie folk band The Decemberists. It’s an intense and often violent display of puppetry with a third act that resembles a “Lord of the Rings” war sequence. But even so Burke said the film had a strong showing from the under 34 crowd and a good mix of tweens coming along with their parents. It even received a 5-star grade from the parents’ guide Common Sense Media . These are the types of fans Laika needs to cultivate to get them to revisit their older titles and keep them excited as the company is set to expand into live-action films and whatever other passion project Travis Knight has cooking next.

“People have just really recognized from the get go this is an extraordinary undertaking, and there’s been a real sense that everyone is willing for us to succeed, and I think that is something that we don’t take lightly,” Burke said. “We have a responsibility to make sure that this film gets seen by the widest possible audience, and that’s why I’m so focused on the next couple of weeks, but also its afterlife and what its legacy looks like.”

article_text:
A news item by ArtThrob Editors on the 29th of September 2026. This should take you < 1 minutes to read.

A new exhibition centers young people living around the Mau Forest to create rewilded visions for 2099.

‘Mau: A Forest Imaginarium’ , opening in Nairobi on 17th October 2026, presents a speculative world created during an eight-week Safari Studio by Kairos Futura in and around Masese, on the edge of Kenya’s Mau Forest.

Through drawing, printmaking, sculpture, wearable design, installation, and collective storytelling, participants have imagined the Mau of 2099, with an exhibition that presents a fragment of that imagined future.

The exhibition grows out of The Safari Studio, Kairos Futura’s travelling arts and futures programme. The project works with young people living around landscapes of major ecological importance, using art and speculative worldbuilding as tools for thinking beyond the immediate pressures of the present.

Ideas developed during the studio range from new relationships between people and elephants, rituals, forest technologies, forms of forest protection, healing spaces and new ways of living within a recovering ecosystem.

About Kairos Futura

Kairos Futura is an arts futurist organisation working across Kenya and internationally to explore how imagination can become a practical tool for ecological and social change.

Its programmes combine immersive storytelling, speculative design, visual art, making and field-based learning to create spaces where young people can investigate possible futures for the places they live. Through projects including The Safari Studio, Wild Future Lab, Jungle Room and other experimental arts and futures programmes, Kairos Futura works at the intersection of culture, ecology and future-making.

article_text:
One thing I know is true: You want Carrie Coon on your podcast.

The Emmy-nominated “White Lotus,” “Gilded Age,” and “The Leftovers” star has made plenty of impact on TV playing strong-willed characters. But she’s also a magnetic presence on the big screen, from films like Sean Durkin’s sizzling ’80s marriage satire “The Nest” and Azazel Jacobs’ Bergmanesque sibling drama “His Three Daughters” to her latest film , Guy Nattiv’s “ The Liberation .” In this film, she’s more vulnerable onscreen than ever.

But as dark as Coon can go — in the ’80s-set “The Liberation,” she plays a repressed, PTSD-addled Holocaust survivor brought under the sway of a hypnotic cult leader played by Lily James — she’s a delight to chat with. No topics are off limits. She joined this week’s episode of IndieWire’s “ Screen Talk ” podcast to dive into “The Liberation,” but also to talk about life after “White Lotus” as an actor who is (her joke!) “top of the B list.”

“What I mean is if there are five films coming out in a year that have female leads, we know the five actresses who will be asked to play those parts,” Coon said. ‘And they’re warranted, they’re very talented, they deserve to be in that position. That just means, though, because there are so few, there aren’t very many left over for the rest of us to take a crack at. So it is unusual for me to get this opportunity. I had an opportunity to play the lead in a mainstream film, which was ‘The Nest’ … and it came out during COVID, and nobody saw it. And so it didn’t necessarily open the doors we hoped. Showing I could carry a film, that didn’t really happen for me with ‘The Nest.’ And so it was just very flattering to get a script [for ‘The Liberation’] like this come into my inbox.”

This time, though, Coon’s extraordinary performance in “The Liberation” could open the doors “The Nest” didn’t. (Distributor Bleecker Street is launching a qualifying run next week.)

Coon also talked about co-starring with her real-life husband Tracy Letts, who plays her “Liberation” character Rita’s husband in Nattiv’s film, and Letts’ infamously obsessive physical media collection — and how that’s trickling down to their two kids’ intrepid viewing habits.

Though first up, hear banter from me and my co-host Anne Thompson about our time at the Virginia Film Festival, awards season updates, and more.

Listen to the episode below or on your preferred podcast platform.

The film arrives in theaters on October 30 and on Netflix on November 18 ."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Look into my eyes / can you see they’re open wide / would I lie to you?” Those lyrics linger in the air as a soft whisper for only a moment before the accompanying piano notes carry them away and into the beginning of Gentle Monster , the latest from Corsage director Marie Kreutzer. Note: This review was originally published as part of our 2026 Cannes coverage. The film arrives in theaters on October 30 and on Netflix on November 18 .

“Look into my eyes / can you see they’re open wide / would I lie to you?” Those lyrics linger in the air as a soft whisper for only a moment before the accompanying piano notes carry them away and into the beginning of Gentle Monster , the latest from Corsage director Marie Kreutzer. One might already suspect that the cover of such an emblematic ’90s pop song, pulsating under the fingertips of the film’s protagonist, Lucy (Léa Seydoux), could serve as exposition in some way. Yet the growl camouflaged in Seydoux’s silky voice might just as well be a sign of fatigue—the Lucy we meet in this opening scene is still adapting to quiet, countryside life from a career of touring European capitals. When her husband Philip (Laurence Rupp) interrupts her practice by rushing in, full-on panic attack, it’s the patience in her consoling voice that signals it’s not the first time she has stopped mid-song to make room for him.

Somewhere in the Austrian hills, a big house with an even bigger garden offers Lucy, Phillip, and their little boy Johnny (Malo Blanchet) a new start––in the boxes, naked walls, and all one sees is a life being unpacked, slowly but surely. Kreutzer’s script reveals very little directly: fleeting references to Philip’s burnout being the reason to move are countered by the joy with which he holds up a Super-8 camera to document a new chapter in their familial life. Scenes of domestic bliss flicker in the reels as the only real testament to his career as a filmmaker—except for a poster of Bergman’s Persona propped against the wall—in a gesture that feels already like a slight. Instead of taking the opportunity to weave a meta-narrative around an artistic couple and their mysterious decline, Kreutzer refuses to characterize Philip or his work. At the same time, we’re given glimpses of Lucy’s career as an avant-garde concert pianist who solely covers songs by male artists in front of rapt audiences.

Yes, Gentle Monster ‘s perspective is female in the sense that the audience has more access to Lucy’s psychology, but in the second act, Kreutzer splits the perspective by introducing us to a character who has been secondary until then: police officer Elsa Kühn (Jella Haase), who delivers a search warrant at the narrative’s start. When proceedings swerve to Elsa’s life off the clock, we see a hyperindependent woman with an ageing, ailing father who tends to be inappropriate with the live-in nurse, and matching that, Haase’s performance is as stoic as you’d expect from any lead in a police procedural. Lensed by cinematographer Judith Kaufmann ( The Teacher’s Lounge, Corsage ), the film looks crisp and exposing in its static, wide-shot scenes, countered by the intimate soundtrack from French artist Camille.

Gentle Monster marks the Austrian filmmaker’s return to psychological drama / thriller territory of 2019’s The Ground Beneath My Feet , but the former wouldn’t exist if it wasn’t for the genre-bending Corsage . In fact, a turn of events following the completion of the her-story period film became the real-life basis for Kreutzer’s new script. Saying any more would reveal perhaps a bit too much about plot than intended, but if the reader is already familiar with a certain scandal that shook the Austrian film industry in 2023, they wouldn’t be surprised by the plot twist that comes early in Gentle Monster , whose title refers to Philip’s character. Rupp, who’s primarily known for his TV roles and 2024’s absurdist comedy Veni Vidi Vici, carries the heavy load for the role of a tortured man whose desperation and resentment are cloaked in love. His face remains expressionless and hard to read throughout as the relationship with Lucy strains and snaps, and no amount of sorries can wash off the stench of secrets he exudes in every scene.

Léa Seydoux, on the other hand, almost carries the film’s emotional weight like a crown––rather than self-congratulatory, the confidence she radiates as Lucy comes across as a genuine belief that things may not be so bad after all. Even if the plot is one of subdued melodrama picking at the male-inflicted wounds of women, both Seydoux and Haase embody a degree of relatable pretense to spare the men who hurt them while simmering with rage on the inside. For all its measuredness, Gentle Monster is a merciless film, not so much to the viewers but its titular character––a gesture some may deem exaggerated, yet there is a tenderness that steers Kreutzer’s script away from revenge, humiliation, or brutal punishment. For its taboo subject matter, this already says a lot.

Gentle Monster premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival.

El protagonista de The Pitt recibió el reconocimiento de la revista People a los 55 años, tras consagrarse con importantes premios por su trabajo en la serie médica.

Noah Wyle recibió el galardón por la revista People como el hombre vivo más sexy de 2026. El actor, reconocido por sus papeles en ER y The Pitt , recibió la noticia con sorpresa y admitió que nunca imaginó obtener esta distinción. “ Pensé que era una broma; ni en un millón de años habría pensado que este sería un honor otorgado a mí ”, confesó en una entrevista con la publicación.

El reconocimiento llega en uno de los mejores momentos de su carrera, impulsado por su papel del doctor Michael “Robby” Robinavitch en The Pitt , el drama médico de HBO que se convirtió en uno de los grandes éxitos televisivos de 2025. Su actuación le valió dos premios Emmy consecutivos como mejor actor en una serie dramática, en 2025 y 2026, además de un Globo de Oro en 2026.

La familia detrás del actor

La reacción de su familia también formó parte de la celebración. Su esposa, Sara, lo ayudó a dimensionar el reconocimiento, mientras que sus hijos Owen, de 24 años, y Auden, de 21, reaccionaron entre la sorpresa y las bromas. Frances, su hija menor, de 11 años, también participó en la sesión fotográfica de People , en la que Wyle mostró su faceta más cotidiana al preparar huevos, limpiar la cocina y doblar ropa.

View this post on Instagram

La carrera del actor despegó en 1994, cuando se incorporó a ER para interpretar al doctor John Carter, personaje al que dio vida durante 15 años, hasta el final de la serie en 2009. Después participó en producciones como Falling Skies , antes de recuperar el protagonismo con The Pitt . La tercera temporada de la serie médica tiene previsto su estreno en enero de 2027.

Wyle sucede a Jonathan Bailey , protagonista de Wicked , quien obtuvo el título en 2025 y se convirtió en el primer hombre abiertamente gay en recibirlo. El reconocimiento de People se entrega desde 1985, cuando el elegido fue Mel Gibson. A lo largo de sus 41 ediciones, la distinción también se le otorgó a figuras como Patrick Dempsey, Chris Evans, Paul Rudd, Michael B. Jordan e Idris Elba .

2026年11月3日、皇居三の丸尚蔵館（東京都千代田区）がついにグランドオープンしました。 東京・奈良・京都・九州に続く「5番目の国立博物館」として、久しぶりに誕生した国立博物館です。 プレオープンから美術ファンにメッセージを送ってくれてきた島谷館長が今回もグランドオープン記念特別展「皇室の至宝―美いづるところ」を案内してくれました。 書を専門とする館長が紹介するのは、館収蔵の国宝《雲紙本和漢朗詠集》です。宮中の宴で朗詠するために選ばれた和歌と漢詩は、現代なら「高級カラオケ」と分かりやすく解説。ダイナミックな筆づかいや、雲を斜めに配した料紙のデザインにも注目です。 また今回の特別展「皇室の至宝」の前期（11月23日まで）では、皇居の中で初めて正倉院宝物（「螺鈿紫檀琵琶」など）が一般公開されています。 完全予約制のため、人越しではなく、ゆっくりと名品と向き合うことができます。ぜひ実際に足を運んでご覧ください。 （撮影編集：読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班 岡本公樹）

Films and events

Love

In a Whisper

À Voix basse

When a young queer woman returns home to Tunisia to mourn her uncle’s death, she finds his cause of death shrouded in mystery.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Leyla Bouzid

With Eya Bouteraa, Hiam Abbass, Marion Barbeau

France-Tunisia 2026. 113min

Courtesy of Playtime

Languages Arabic, French With English subtitles

Introduction

Returning to her intergenerational matriarchal household, Lilia notices everyone – including herself – is keeping secrets. But as she pries into what happened to her uncle, she must decide if she is finally ready to reveal parts of herself to her loved ones. Leyla Bouzid’s latest film is a sumptuous family drama about lineage and queerness.

Grace Barber-Plentie

With thanks to Unifrance.

Content advice

Contains homophobic attitudes and language.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Sweet Milk Lake

In writer-director-actor Harvey Zielinski’s coming-of-age drama, a young trans man’s homecoming results in unexpected consequences when he’s mistaken for his cisgender twin brother.

Ben’Imana

This Cannes Camera d’Or winner unfolds in the shadow of the 1994 Rwandan genocide, exploring its legacy and the possibility of forgiveness.

Fruit Gathering

Writer-director Aung Phyoe’s enthralling, visually striking drama charts a homoerotic friendship between two young Burmese women.

article_text:
パナソニック汐留美術館 は、フランスの画家ジョルジュ・ルオーの常設展示のほか、「建築・住まい」「工芸・デザイン」をテーマとした企画展を開催している。このたび、同館で2027年に開催される展覧会のラインアップが発表された。3つの展覧会を見どころとあわせて紹介する。

スウェーデンのうつわ グスタフスベリのある暮らし／2027年1月16日〜3月22日

グスタフスベリは、1825年に設立されたスウェーデンを代表する陶磁器メーカー。本展は、同社を代表する4人のデザイナー、 ヴィルヘルム・コーゲ 、 スティグ・リンドベリ 、 リサ・ラーソン 、 カーリン・ビョルクヴィスト に焦点を当て、スウェーデン国立美術館所蔵の約300点を紹介する。あわせて、スウェーデン王立工科大学に留学した浅子雄祐（SPROUTZ Studio）による「光」をテーマとした空間演出も見どころだ。

ひろしま美術館コレクション 美の交響 ―フランス近代美術と日本洋画の100年―／2027年4月10日〜6月20日

19世紀半ばから20世紀前半にかけてのフランス美術の変革は、一定の時間差を伴いながら日本へと伝わった。日本の洋画家たちは、それを受けて独自の油彩画を展開した。本展は、ひろしま美術館のコレクションから、バルビゾン派からエコール・ド・パリに至るフランス近代美術と、日本近代洋画を同一空間に展示する。クロード・モネ、ポール・セザンヌ、ポール・ゴーギャン、アンリ・マティス、黒田清輝、安井曾太郎らの作品が一堂に会する。

Dancing Bauhaus, Beyond 踊るバウハウス、その先へ（仮）／2027年7月15日〜9月23日

本展は、20世紀の芸術・デザイン史に大きな転換をもたらしたバウハウスを起点に、その理念と実践が現代の造形文化のなかでどのように展開してきたかを紹介する。 武蔵野美術大学 美術館・図書館 との2館共同企画で、同館がオスカー・シュレンマーの創作活動を紹介するのに対し、パナソニック汐留美術館は「身体と空間」という主題に着目する。エットレ・ソットサス、倉俣史朗、三宅一生らの実践を通して、バウハウスの理念と活動をたどる。

また、2027年秋には女性建築家をテーマとした建築展を開催する予定。戦前から戦後にかけて日本の建築が飛躍的に発展した最初期の女性建築家にフォーカスし、近代建築史上の彼女たちの成果や功績、周辺領域のクリエイターにも焦点を当てる。会期は2027年10月16日〜12月19日。
